rows.why: Byte-for-byte the same four-line explanation of why an escaped invalid-UTF-8 argument is accepted, copy-pasted above two different tests in the same file (defs.rs:1297 and :1938), with no wording changed at all.

The same six-line rationale for precomputing per-match locations was copied from one printer sink into the other (json.rs vs standard.rs); only a trailing parenthetical about the extra replacement search was appended, so the shared prose is copied wording, not independent writing.
Identical text to the character between defs.rs:1938 and defs.rs:2034 — the same escaped-invalid-UTF-8 explanation pasted a third time above another flag's test.

A test comment including its ASCII directory-tree diagram was copy-pasted for the sibling test and edited by a few characters only (".git directory" to ".git *file*" for submodules, ".git/" to ".git"); the surviving prose is copied verbatim rather than rewritten.
The identical six-line paragraph explaining why a raw invalid-UTF-8 flag value fails the UTF-8 check appears unchanged at defs.rs:1948 and defs.rs:2044 above two analogous separator-flag tests.
Third pairing of the same word-identical escaped-invalid-UTF-8 comment (defs.rs:1297 vs :2034), so the same text now exists at three sites in one file.
Word-identical copy of the "we specifically try to pass an invalid UTF-8 argument" paragraph at defs.rs:1304 and :2044; nothing distinguishes the two spans textually.
Same paragraph again, unchanged, at defs.rs:1304 and :1948 — completing the third-occurrence triangle of one copy-pasted test rationale.

retired.why: The two crate-level rustdocs describe completely different crates (printers vs line-oriented searcher); the overlap is the verbatim SHERLOCK doctest fixture — the same six-line Conan Doyle excerpt embedded as a byte-string corpus in both examples — plus the shared rustdoc template headings, and that embedded common source is the bulk of the shared characters.

doc_gaps.note: The six defs.rs spans stop exactly at the comment and exclude the test body below, so the segments carry no trace of which flag each test exercises; the only thing that distinguishes these otherwise byte-identical spans lies outside the span boundaries.

The span covers the whole 58-line module doc, so a fenced runnable doctest (including the SHERLOCK byte-string fixture and assert_eq! lines) is folded into what is measured as documentation prose; the same is true of the 82-line searcher/src/lib.rs span.
